chunk_findings.detail: The hook wiring only adds `N.for_hook(...)` for `session_start` and `prompt`; the manifest shows no added nudge call in any `SubagentStop` or `Stop` hook handler. Given the stated regression scenario — a `SubagentStop` hook payload with free slots and ready items — the installed hook path will not produce a nudge, so the master session is not told to refill the pipeline when a subagent finishes. The pipeline will not refill without an operator prompt unless the user next triggers `UserPromptSubmit`, contrary to the stated intent and the hook set named in the intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/hooks.py:_on_session_start/_on_prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `_on_prompt` accepts `dry_run` but ignores it: unlike `_on_session_start`, it calls `N.for_hook(repo, "prompt", agent)` unconditionally. Because the new nudge service is responsible for persisted cooldown/dedup state (`state_path`, `load_state`, `save_state`) and `for_hook` receives no dry-run flag, a dry-run `UserPromptSubmit` hook with `[dispatch].nudge = true` and a newly startable plan can record the nudge fingerprint/cooldown as if it had been shown. The subsequent real prompt then receives no nudge even though the dry run should have had no observable effect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/hooks.py:243 _on_prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The cooldown is bypassed whenever a hook call is quiet. A shown hint stores `{"fp": "A", "at": 0}`. If a later call has `free <= 0` or no ready items, the quiet branch clears `fp` but keeps `at`. A different line produced at `now=20` with `cooldown_s=1200` is then returned because the cooldown check is gated on `state.get("fp")`, which is now empty. Thus a transient no-ready state resets the cooldown, and ready-state flicker can produce nudges on alternating prompts despite the configured cooldown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/dispatch/nudge.py:decide

chunk_findings.detail: The `max_chars` truncation can return a hint longer than `max_chars`. For example, with `max_chars=2` and any text longer than 2, line 72 computes `text[:max(0, -1)] + "..."`, returning `"..."`, whose length is 3; the same happens for `max_chars=1`. If the knob is set to a positive value below 3, the emitted hook line violates the configured maximum length.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/dispatch/nudge.py:decide

chunk_findings.detail: The stated regression test is for a SubagentStop hook payload, but this file only exercises the UserPromptSubmit handler (`_on_prompt`) and the generic helpers with event `"prompt"`. Given a SubagentStop payload with free slots and ready items, the suite would still pass if `ddflow.api.setup.hooks` never calls `N.for_hook` for SubagentStop, calls it with the wrong event, or fails to inject the returned context, because no test constructs a SubagentStop payload or asserts the resulting hook response. Thus the required “SubagentStop produces one nudge; same state produces none” behavior is not actually covered.
